script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: Redemption on the Field

FADE IN:

INT. MORNING SUNLIGHT - HOME OFFICE - DAY

JOHN, mid-40s, disheveled, hunched over a laptop, his eyes red from lack of sleep. His office is cluttered with papers, empty coffee cups, and pizza boxes.

JOHN (whispering to himself)
Come on, John. You can do this.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL FIELD - DAY

Flashback to younger JOHN, tanned, muscular, grinning as he leads his team to victory.

INT. MORNING SUNLIGHT - HOME OFFICE - DAY

Back in the present, John's phone rings.

John: (answering) Hello?

PRINCIPAL JENKINS (V.O.)
John, I need to see you in my office as soon as possible.

INT. PRINCIPAL'S OFFICE - DAY

John sits nervously across from Principal Jenkins.

PRINCIPAL JENKINS
John, I've received some troubling news. The school district is cutting funding for the athletic program. If we can't come up with a way to save it, we'll have to disband the football team.

INT. JOHN'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

John paces in front of the fireplace, deep in thought.

Suddenly, an idea strikes him. He grabs his phone and dials a number.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - DAY

Int. Coffee Shop - Day

MRS. JOHNSON, late 50s, sits at a table, sipping a cup of coffee. John enters.

JOHN
Mrs. Johnson, I need your help.

MRS. JOHNSON
(surprised)
John, it's been a long time. What can I do for you?

JOHN
We need to save the football program at the high school. They're going to disband it due to budget cuts.

MRS. JOHNSON
(thoughtful)
I see. And what makes you think I can help?

JOHN
Because you're the best football coach this town has ever seen.

MRS. JOHNSON
(smiling)
Well, I'll consider it. But it won't be easy.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL GYM - DAY

Mrs. Johnson enters the gym, where a group of disinterested students gather. She begins to lead them in a rigorous workout.

INT. PRINCIPAL'S OFFICE - DAY

John and Principal Jenkins discuss the progress of the team.

PRINCIPAL JENKINS
John, I've never seen these kids so motivated. But we still need funding.

JOHN
Leave that to me.

INT. JOHN'S HOME OFFICE - NIGHT

John spends long hours researching and drafting a business plan for the team.

INT. COMMUNITY CENTER - DAY

John and Mrs. Johnson present their business plan to a group of potential investors.

INVESTOR 1
(skeptical)
Sports teams don't exactly have the best track record for profitability.

MRS. JOHNSON
(passionate)
But this team is different. These kids deserve a second chance.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL FIELD - NIGHT

The team practices under the moonlit sky, determined to make the season a success.

INT. PRINCIPAL'S OFFICE - DAY

Principal Jenkins informs John that they've secured enough funding to keep the team alive.

JOHN
(relieved)
We did it.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL GAME - DAY

The team plays their first game against a rival school. Despite initial setbacks, they pull together and win in a dramatic finish.

INT. HIGH SCHOOL FOOTBALL FIELD - NIGHT

John and Mrs. Johnson watch the jubilant team celebrate their victory.

MRS. JOHNSON
(teary-eyed)
We did it, John. We gave these kids a second chance.

FADE OUT.
